notes: A song that stops a second or two after you press play is put back again. The app remembers an interruption — a call, another app taking the audio — and it never forgot it, so every later stop was believed instead of undone and a song could stay parked at 0:02 waiting for you.

Pressing play is you asking for sound, whichever way you press it: the app’s own button, the lock screen, the notification, the widget. All of them end that memory now, so the app stops protecting a song that nothing is holding.

An outside pause in the first seconds of a song is no longer obeyed. The guard that refuses a stale lock-screen pause gave up after 1.2 seconds — shorter than the hand-over with the phone’s media session takes — and covers the first four seconds now, recording what it refused.

The "playback stopped while it was starting" banner no longer switches the audio-focus helper off. It has not asked for audio focus since 58.8.4, so it is not in the play path, and switching it off only cost the app its call detection and the assistant duck. It stays on.

That banner also stops appearing for a page that simply reloaded itself, which is what an update hand-over and a refresh are. The app now asks the browser whether this boot is a reload, and a reload is never reported as a crash.
A death during "starting playback" is still recorded, and still says so once, in plain words, instead of stacking two messages on the screen.
